Enable or disable client-side cache invalidation. Invalidations reach a RESP3 connection as push messages; a RESP2 connection has to `REDIRECT` them to a connection subscribed to `__redis__:invalidate`, and without `REDIRECT` is sent nothing, as in Redis. Every key a command reads is tracked, and keys written by scripts, expired, evicted or flushed are invalidated. Default mode: all reads auto-register; writers receive their own invalidations. OPTIN: only reads preceded by `CLIENT CACHING yes` are registered. OPTOUT: all reads register unless preceded by `CLIENT CACHING no`. NOLOOP: suppress invalidations sent back to the client that caused the write. REDIRECT forwards invalidations to another client ID. Zero cost when no tracking clients connected — one atomic load per command on the hot path

documented.notes: Block until `numreplicas` replicas have acknowledged all preceding writes, or `timeout` milliseconds elapse; returns the number of replicas that acked
Block until the local AOF has fsynced all preceding writes, or `timeout` milliseconds elapse; returns `[local_fsynced, replica_fsynced]`
Mark keys for optimistic locking; must be called before `MULTI`
Acknowledge processed entries; removes from PEL

Acknowledge and delete entries in one step (Redis 8.2). Per id: `-1` not pending in this group, `1` acknowledged and deleted (or already gone), `2` acknowledged but kept because another group still references it (`ACKED` only). Policies as for `XDELEX`. The bare form `XACKDEL key group id [id ...]` is still accepted
documented.syntax: XACKDEL key group [KEEPREF | DELREF | ACKED] IDS numids id [id ...]

documented.notes: Append an entry; `*` auto-generates ID as `ms-seq`; NOMKSTREAM skips creation if key absent; MAXLEN/MINID trim the stream after insert, and `KEEPREF` / `DELREF` / `ACKED` say what trimming does with entries consumer groups still reference. `IDMP` / `IDMPAUTO` (Redis 8.6) make the add idempotent: a retry by the same producer with the same id — or, with `IDMPAUTO`, the same content — adds nothing and returns the original entry's ID
documented.syntax: XADD key [NOMKSTREAM] [KEEPREF | DELREF | ACKED] [IDMPAUTO producer-id | IDMP producer-id idempotent-id] [MAXLEN|MINID [=|~] threshold [LIMIT count]] *|id field value [...]

documented.notes: Scan and claim idle pending entries starting from `start`
documented.syntax: XAUTOCLAIM key group consumer min-idle-time start [COUNT count] [JUSTID]

documented.notes: Set per-stream configuration; supported fields: `MAX-ENTRIES n` (persistent trim policy applied on every XADD, `0` clears the policy), `MAX-DELETED-ENTRY-ID id` (advance the tracked max deleted ID, never moves backwards), `IDMP-DURATION seconds` and `IDMP-MAXSIZE n` (how long, and how many, idempotent ids are remembered per producer; defaults from `stream-idmp-duration` / `stream-idmp-maxsize`)
Claim ownership of pending entries idle longer than min-idle-time
documented.syntax: XCLAIM key group consumer min-idle-time id [id ...] [IDLE ms] [TIME ms] [RETRYCOUNT n] [FORCE] [JUSTID] [LASTID id]

documented.notes: Delete entries by ID; returns count deleted

Delete entries with control over consumer-group references (Redis 8.2). Per id: `-1` no such entry, `1` deleted, `2` kept because a group still references it (`ACKED` only). `KEEPREF` (default) deletes and leaves pending-list references; `DELREF` deletes and removes them from every group; `ACKED` deletes only an entry every group has read and acknowledged. The policy may also follow the `IDS` block; `REF` is accepted as an older name for `ACKED`
documented.syntax: XDELEX key [KEEPREF | DELREF | ACKED] IDS numids id [id ...]

documented.notes: Create a consumer group; `$` starts from the latest entry; MKSTREAM creates the key if absent
documented.syntax: XGROUP CREATE key group id|$ [MKSTREAM] [ENTRIESREAD n]

Delete a consumer group and its PEL
Set the group's last-delivered ID, and optionally its entries-read counter

List consumer groups with metadata
Return stream metadata
Return the number of entries

Release pending entries back to the group PEL without acknowledging, for immediate re-delivery. SILENT decrements the delivery counter, FAIL leaves it, FATAL pins it to LLONG_MAX; RETRYCOUNT overrides. FORCE creates unowned entries for non-pending IDs that exist in the stream
documented.syntax: XNACK key group <SILENT | FAIL | FATAL> IDS numids id [id ...] [RETRYCOUNT count] [FORCE]

documented.notes: Return pending entry summary or detail list

documented.notes: Return entries with IDs in `[start, end]`; `-` and `+` are open bounds; bare `ms` expands to `ms-0` / `ms-MAXSEQ`

Read new entries across multiple streams; `$` means entries added after this call and `+` the last entry; BLOCK suspends until new data arrives or timeout. `COUNT` is per stream; `MAXCOUNT` and `MAXSIZE` (Redis 8.10) cap the entries and the bytes of the whole reply
documented.syntax: XREAD [COUNT count] [MAXCOUNT maxcount] [MAXSIZE maxsize] [BLOCK ms] STREAMS key [key ...] id [id ...]

documented.notes: Read new (`>`) or pending (specific ID) entries for a consumer; NOACK skips PEL tracking. `CLAIM` (Redis 8.4) also takes over entries pending for other consumers that have been idle that long, ahead of new ones; every entry then carries its idle time and delivery count. A group that does not exist is a `NOGROUP` error
documented.syntax: XREADGROUP GROUP group consumer [COUNT n] [MAXCOUNT n] [MAXSIZE n] [BLOCK ms] [CLAIM min-idle-time] [NOACK] STREAMS key [key ...] id [id ...]

documented.notes: Same as XRANGE but in reverse order
Set the stream's last-generated ID and metadata

Trim stream by length or minimum ID. With `~` trimming is approximate, removing whole nodes of `stream-node-max-entries` entries, and `LIMIT` caps how many are removed (an error without `~`, as in Redis). `KEEPREF` (default) leaves consumer groups' pending references to trimmed entries, `DELREF` removes them, `ACKED` stops at the first entry not yet acknowledged by every group
documented.syntax: XTRIM key MAXLEN|MINID [=|~] threshold [LIMIT count] [KEEPREF | DELREF | ACKED]
